# Dedication & Preface

## Dedication

To every couple and every soul seeking covenant clarity — that the light of creation may once again define love, and that fidelity, rightly lived, may restore the foundation of civilization.

## Preface

This book opens at first principles because confusion about marriage has multiplied while clarity has grown scarce. Sex by Design (SBD) restores clarity by returning to design—what God made, what Scripture declares, what nature itself reveals, and what a sane society must protect if it intends to flourish. We name that flourishing eudaemonia: a life that is whole, abundant, steady and good. Marriage is not a lifestyle accessory. It is a creation-ordained institution for mature men and women, the generator of family, and family is the fundamental group unit of society. Distort marriage and you diminish the family; diminish the family and you weaken the nation. SBD therefore insists on literacy, maturity, and fidelity—not as slogans, but as habits that align with reality.

# Chapter 1 — Entry: Modern Societal Eudaemonia: The Marriage Handbook for Human Flourishing

## 1.1 Dianoetic Modus Ponens — “Come, Let Us Reason”

“Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.”

> *— Isaiah 1:18 (KJV)*

The SBD path begins where Scripture invites us to begin: reason. We do not outsource marriage to fashion, politics, or trend. We submit marriage to design and reason from fixed premises:

- P1: Human flourishing requires strong families.

- P2: Strong families require strong marriages.

- C: Therefore, any people serious about flourishing must honor, educate, and guard marriage.

Reason also guards language. “One flesh” (Gen 2:24) is not metaphor-only. It is biological, covenantal, and societal reality. When the foundation is honored, wholeness follows.

## 1.2 Disavowal — Truth Over Trends

SBD disavows the culture-bound idea that marriage is whatever a momentary consensus says it is. We reject the myth that marriage fixes brokenness. Marriage is not therapy; it is covenant. And covenant presumes maturity. Your spouse is not your “better half”; they are your better whole. The equation of covenant is never 0.5 + 0.5; it is 1 + 1 → one flesh. Literacy matters because the mis-educated will mis-live. SBD is education in the right order of things so life may be lived well.

## 1.3 Eudaemonia — the Goal of Human Life in God

Eudaemonia (human flourishing) is not mere comfort. In Scripture it resonates with shalom—wholeness, integrity, fruitfulness, peace, productive life. “I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.”

> *— John 10:10 (KJV)*

Abundance is not decadence; it is order, joy, and fruitfulness. Within marriage, pleasure is not suspicious; it is by design. Pleasure is not an idol to be worshiped nor a shame to be hidden; it is a gift to be stewarded in covenant.

## 1.4 Design — Male and Female in the Image of God

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”

> *— Genesis 1:27 (KJV)*

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh. And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.”

> *— Genesis 2:24–25 (KJV)*

Design precedes doctrine. Male and female is not an afterthought; it is how humanity images God in the twobecome-one covenant. Their union is inherently conjugal and covenantal—a unity of difference that yields fruit and fellowship. “Naked and not ashamed” is the original normal of covenant clarity, not a modern scandal.

## 1.5 Practice From Perfection — Your Worth Is Pre-Given

“Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.”

> *— Romans 3:24 (KJV)*

SBD replaces the anxiety of “practice makes perfect” with Practice From Perfection. In Christ, you are restored to wholeness so that you can practice habits that match your real identity. We practice not to earn worth, but to steward the worth we have been given. This matters in marriage: performance-driven marriages calcify; identity-driven marriages breathe. Starter Habits in Practice From Perfection

- Identity first: speak to your spouse as a whole person, not a problem to be fixed.

- Consent-first: curiosity and kindness fuel covenant; coercion breaks it.

- A3 Mini-Loop: Attitude → Attire → Allure (carry yourself warmly; dress with intention; extend welcome).

## 1.6 Marriage Is Not Growth But Maturation

Marriage is not a laboratory for self-discovery; it is an institution designed for those who are already mature. Growth is for childhood; marriage is for adults who have matured into wholeness. “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.”

> *— Hebrews 5:14 (KJV)*

Therefore: marriage requires men and women of full age—whole in development, mature in discernment, and capable of covenantal responsibility. UDHR Article 16(1): “Men and women of full age, without any limitation due to race, nationality or religion, have the right to marry and to found a family.” This secular affirmation aligns with Scripture’s moral architecture: full age → covenant capacity. Maturation comes before vows. Two whole persons enter; oneness is the fruit. Diagnostic: Are We Whole Yet?

- Behavioral: self-command; you keep your word even when it costs.

- Temperamental: steadiness; you can hold tension without rage or retreat.

- Emotional: empathy; you feel with and for your spouse without manipulation.

- Mental: discernment; you reason soundly about covenant, sex, and duty.

If these are undeveloped, seek maturation first. It is wiser to prepare well than to repair endlessly.

## 1.7 The Public Good of Marriage

UDHR Article 16(3): “The family is the natural and fundamental group unit of society and is entitled to protection by society and the State.” Scripture taught it first; nations acknowledge it for survival. Strong marriages make strong families; strong families uphold civilization. Public policy that undermines marriage invites civic fragility. Public policy that protects marriage builds national durability.

Implications

- Schools, churches, and states should teach marriage literacy.

- Cultural industries should honor the marriage bed rather than mock it.

- Communities should support couples with education, mentoring, and sane rites of passage.

## 1.8 Literacy Before Vows — What SBD Teaches

SBD Literacy Tracks (Entry Level)

- Covenant Foundations: design, duty, delight; “one flesh” as conjugal reality.

- Consent & Conversation: green/yellow/red lists; weekly 15-min check-ins.

- A3 Expression: attitude, attire, allure—how presence builds attraction.

- Muliebrity & Virility: feminine and masculine competencies (appearance, speech, service, steadiness).

- Fidelity Habits: tender pursuit, timing, exclusivity, celebration.

- Practice From Perfection: identity-driven routines; six-week starter plan.

Why Before Vows? - Because maturity precedes covenant. Literate couples thrive; incurious couples drift.

## 1.9 The One-Flesh Logic (PREVIEW of Chapter 5)

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.”

> *— Genesis 2:24 (KJV)*

“What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.”

> *— 1 Corinthians 6:16 (KJV)*

SBD affirms a truth many evade: oneness is covenantal and conjugal. Paper records vows; habits keep them. This book will later argue in depth that sex belongs to marriage, and marriage is sustained by conjugal fidelity. But here, at the foundation, learn the logic: the body speaks covenant; therefore literacy in conjugal life is part of marital duty.

## 1.10 Mini-Map for the Six-Week Starter (PREVIEW)

- Week 1: Shared glossary; two 15-minute check-ins.

- Week 2: A3 mini-experiment (attire + atmosphere).

- Week 3: Listening date + daily appreciations.

- Week 4: Weekly “practice session” (consent-first, kind, unhurried).

- Week 5: Comfort & curiosity lists (build, compare, plan).

- Week 6: Review, celebrate, and choose the next SBD book.

(Full plan appears in Chapter 11: Practice From Perfection.)

## 1.11 Exercises & Dialogues

Reflection (Personal)

- Copy Genesis 2:24–25 in your journal. Underline “one flesh” and “not ashamed.” What do these require of you?

- Define maturity in your own words using Hebrews 5:14. Where are you strong? Where do you need training?

- Write your A3 (Attitude–Attire–Allure) intention for the next two weeks.

Dialogue (Couple)

- Share three hopes you have for your marriage that depend on maturity, not luck.

- Build green/yellow/red lists together (comforts, curiosities, and boundaries).

- Design a weekly ritual that says, “We honor our covenant” (e.g., Friday night blessing, Sunday gratitude).

## 1.12 Key Terms (MINI Lexical)

- Eudaemonia: Human flourishing; wholeness, fruitfulness, peace.

- Covenant: A vowed union sealed and expressed in conjugal oneness.

- Muliebrity: The state and trait of womanly strength, grace, and aesthetic wisdom.

- Virility: The state and trait of manly steadiness, service, and headship by design.

- Practice From Perfection: Habits that flow from identity restored, not from anxiety to earn worth.

## 1.13 Frequently Asked (ENTRY-LEVEL)

Q: “If marriage requires wholeness, what if we’re still growing?” A: Growth continues all life; maturation (full age) means you have enough self-command, steadiness, empathy, and discernment to keep covenant. If these are missing, seek training now—before vows.

Q: “Is pleasure suspect?” A: Pleasure is not an enemy; disorder is. Within covenant, pleasure is stewarded—never idolized, never suppressed. Q: “Why tie marriage to the public good?” A: Because family is the fundamental group unit (UDHR 16:3). Protect marriage → strengthen families → stabilize society.

## 1.14 Summary & Next Step

- Design: male and female → one flesh → family → society.

- Reason: truth over trend; covenant over fashion.

- Maturity: full age precedes vows (Heb 5:14; UDHR 16:1).

- Flourishing: abundance is ordered joy (Jn 10:10).

- Action: begin Practice From Perfection—small, faithful, weekly habits.

# Chapter 2 — What About Sex? Why Everyone Must Be Sexually Literate

Why Everyone Must Be Sexually Literate

## 2.1 The Uncomfortable Question

The first question that shakes almost every reader of “Sex by Design” is, “What about sex?” We live in a culture saturated with sexual imagery but starved of sexual literacy. Children are groomed by entertainment, adults are confused by shifting norms, and even believers are left unsure of what’s sacred, what’s profane, and what’s simply designed. SBD’s answer is not prudishness, nor permissiveness. It is clarity. Sexuality, in its originative design, is not shameful; it is sacred. But sacred things mishandled bring harm. Therefore, sexual literacy is not optional; it is a moral duty of every adult who hopes to marry, raise children, and sustain civilization.

## 2.2 Sexuality As Birthright, Not Taboo

“And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.”

> *— Genesis 2:25 (KJV)*

At creation, nakedness was normal. Sexual difference was visible. Pleasure was designed. There was no pornographic gaze; there was only honor. In the fall, shame entered, and cultures oscillated between hedonism (everything goes) and asceticism (everything’s bad). SBD calls you back to design:

- Sexuality is anthropogenic (you’re born with it).

- Sexual organs are not mistakes but markers of covenant capacity.

- Pleasure is not punishment but participation in God’s plan for marital oneness.

You don’t need to be “not a nun” to know about sexuality. You are already part of the sexual human story simply by existing. Literacy is stewardship of design.

## 2.3 Sexual Hedonism Defined Correctly

Many recoil at the term hedonism. Yet Revelation 4:11 declares: “Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.”

> *— Revelation 4:11 (KJV)*

God Himself uses pleasure language. The problem is not pleasure but perversion. True sexual hedonism is the devotion to marital pleasure as a matter of ethical stewardship. It honors the anatomical “lock-andkey” complementarity (male–female) and guards fidelity. Misuse of sexuality—same-sex intercourse, promiscuity, porn, infidelity—misplaces the originative meaning of “intercourse.” “Inter-course” literally denotes a between-course—a going between male and female that creates unity and, potentially, life. Deviations cannot replicate that conjugal oneness or generate new life.

## 2.4 Sex = Marriage: the Foundation of Oneness

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.”

> *— Genesis 2:24 (KJV)*

“What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.”

> *— 1 Corinthians 6:16 (KJV)*

These two verses anchor SBD’s philosophy: sex makes oneness, not paper. This does not mean “casual sex = marriage” but that sex consummates and sustains marriage. Paper without fidelity is a shell. Fidelity without paper may be illicit but still forms a “one flesh” bond with real consequences. Therefore, sex belongs inside marriage, because marriage is the public, covenantal frame that protects sex’s private, conjugal power. Outside of marriage, the same act creates harm and soul ties without covenant protection.

## 2.5 The “Wholeness Math”

SBD reframes sexual ethics as simple arithmetic:

- 1 (whole) + 1 (whole) = 2 in covenant becoming one flesh

- Fractional persons (0.5 + 0.5) cannot achieve oneness.

- Sex outside covenant produces broken math: pieces, not peace.

This is why SBD places personal development before vows. Without self-command, temperance, empathy, and discernment, you will misuse the power of sex.

## 2.6 Literacy Before Passion

Why does SBD hammer literacy? Because ignorance breeds misuse. Modern sex education often starts with biology or contraception but ignores meaning. True sexual literacy includes:

- Design Literacy: male/female complementarity, pleasure as stewardship.

- Covenant Literacy: vows, fidelity, exclusivity.

- Body Literacy: cycles, fertility, hygiene, healthy practices.

- Consent & Communication Literacy: green/yellow/red lists; how to talk before you touch.

This literacy prevents abuse, confusion, and shame. It creates space for joy, not guilt.

## 2.7 Sexual Literacy Protects Society

UDHR Article 16(3): “The family is the natural and fundamental group unit of society and is entitled to protection by society and the State.” If family is the fundamental unit, and family begins with marriage, and marriage is consummated and sustained by sex, then sexual literacy is public policy. It is not merely a “private” matter. Ignorant couples create fragile families; fragile families create unstable societies. Nations that teach covenantal sexual literacy produce stronger citizens and lower social costs.

## 2.8 Practical Drills for Sexual Literacy (ENTRY Level)

Individual

- Write out Genesis 2:24 and 1 Corinthians 6:16 in your journal. Underline “one flesh.” Reflect: how does this

redefine sex for you?

- List five ways your current understanding of sexuality has been shaped by culture. Beside each, write the biblical

counter-truth. Couple

- Create your “Green/Yellow/Red” lists:

- Green = welcome, comfortable practices.

- Yellow = curious but cautious.

- Red = off-limits by conviction.

- Practice “Scripture + Conversation” once a week: read a verse on covenant or sexuality, then discuss how to apply it in

your intimacy. Community

- Advocate for real marriage literacy programs in your church or civic space.

- Mentor younger couples; break the silence around covenant and pleasure.

## 2.9 Key Terms (MINI Lexical)

- Sexual Literacy: Stewardship of the design, meaning, and practice of sexuality.

- Anthropogenic Pleasure: Pleasure intrinsic to human design, not acquired externally.

- Covenantal Sex: Intercourse within marriage as both consummation and sustenance of the covenant.

- One-Flesh Reality: The biological, covenantal union of man and wife.

- Green/Yellow/Red Lists: A tool for couples to clarify comfort zones and consent.

## 2.10 Summary & Next Step

- Sex is sacred — designed for covenant.

- Literacy protects pleasure — pleasure without literacy collapses into pain.

- Society needs sexually literate citizens — stable families are a civic good.

# Chapter 3 — How Am I a Part of It? Birthright and Design

## 3.1 The Birthright of Sexual Design

Every man and woman is born into the inheritance of sexuality. It is not something added later in life; it is intrinsic to our very creation. Genesis 1:27 says: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Genesis 2:25 And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed. These verses establishe that our very identity is sexual in design: male and female. To be male or female is not a cultural assignment; it is a divine biological birthright. Just as a child does not earn their family name but receives it at birth, so too we inherit our sexual identity as a stewardship. Herein lies the question: “How am I a part of it?” The answer: because by your anatomy and being alive, you are already “part and parcel” of the sexual design. Sexuality is not a choice or an optional accessory to humanity — it is humanity itself, the protology of humankind.

## 3.2 Stewardship of Design

If sexuality is birthright, then literacy is stewardship. To be sexually illiterate is to mishandle one’s inheritance. Just as a wealthy heir must learn how to manage an estate to preserve it, so every man and woman must learn how to steward their design. Hosea 4:6 warns: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee…”

This applies directly to sexuality. Ignorance leads to destruction — in marriages, families, and societies. Stewardship means:

- Acknowledging design → accepting the reality of male/female complementarity.

- Protecting design → refusing cultural distortions that redefine marriage, sex, or gender against divine order.

- Applying design → living in ways that honor anatomy, fidelity, and covenant.

## 3.3 Anatomy As Participation

The sexual anatomy itself is cogent evidence; The “lock-and-key” design (penis-vagina: male spermatozoon + female ovum) is both symbolic and functional: It defines conjugal-sexual oneness, which is the basis of marriage: oneness by design. 1 Corinthians 6:16 makes this unambiguous: “What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.” If joining with a harlot produces one-flesh reality, how much more is that true within covenant marriage! Thus, the question “How am I a part of it?” is answered by anatomy: simply by being male or female, you are already inescapably part of the sexual epicure — the inheritance of pleasure, procreation, and covenant.

## 3.4 Literacy As Protection of Pleasure

Sexuality is often reduced to danger, shame, or abuse in society. But biblically, its starting point is pleasure. Revelation 4:11 affirms this principle: “Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.” If pleasure is the purpose of creation, then sexuality — designed for covenantal pleasure — must be taught rightly. Literacy protects pleasure from negation, abuse, distortion, and exploitation. Mismanaged pleasure leads to ruin (Romans 1), but stewarded pleasure leads to abundant life (John 10:10).

## 3.5 Personal Development Link

This is where Personal Development: The Roadmap to Maturation interlocks. Sexual literacy is inseparable from personal maturity.

- Behavioral Development → Self-control in action/reaction, necessary for fidelity.

- Temperamental Development → Understanding one’s nature and balancing with covenantal expectations.

- Emotional Development → Building empathy and care to sustain marital affection.

- Mental Development → Reasoning and discernment to protect covenant truth from cultural lies.

Personal maturity (full development) is the basis of sexual literacy , sexuality, and marriage.  That is why UDHR Article 16:1 insists: “Men and women of full age… have the right to marry and to found a family.” “Full age” means maturity — not just biological puberty but developmental wholeness.

## 3.6 Exercises for Reflection

- Birthright Acknowledgment: Write out Genesis 1:27 and journal how your identity as male or female is a divine inheritance, not a cultural construct.

- Stewardship Check: List three ways you can better steward your sexuality (in thought, behavior, or covenant practice).

- Link to Maturity: From the four attributes of personal development (behavioral, temperamental, emotional,

mental), identify which you most need to strengthen before or within marriage. Conclusion To ask “How am I a part of it?” is to awaken to the fact that you already are. By birthright, you are part of humanity’s sexual design. The only question is whether you will steward it faithfully. Participation is not optional — it is ontological. Stewardship, is to manage your inheritance with wisdom, literacy, and covenant fidelity.

# Chapter 4 — The Sexual One and Only: The Anatomy (Epicure Originativeness)

## 4.0 Why Anatomy Matters for Truth

If marriage is a covenant of one flesh, then the language of the body must be understood. Anatomy is not an accident; it is design. The male and female forms are cogent evidence of conjugal purpose: a lock-and-key complementarity that both expresses oneness and—by its very form—can be fruitful. This is what SBD calls Epicure Originativeness: pleasure that originates in design, ordered toward fidelity and fruitfulness. Genesis 1:27 (KJV) “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Genesis 2:24–25 (KJV) “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh. And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.” “Male and female” is not merely a label; it is a calling to conjugal unity. “Naked and not Ashamed” is not license for exhibitionism; it is the original normal of covenantal clarity.

## 4.1 Clarifying Terms (YOUR SBD Lexicon)

- Epicure Originativeness: The origin of marital pleasure in divine design; pleasure that is natural, covenantal,

and ethically ordered.

- Sexual Emblem: The body as sign and instrument of the covenant; the anatomy “speaks” the truth of one flesh.

- Lock-and-Key: Male and female anatomy fit uniquely, forming one act with two inherent meanings: unitive

(oneness) and procreative (ordered to life).

- Hedonism (rightly defined): Devotion to pleasure as stewardship of God’s good design (Rev. 4:11)—never the

idolatry of body or thrill. Revelation 4:11 (KJV) “Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.”

## 4.2 The Body’s Speech: Conjugal Teleology

Teleology means end or purpose. The male and female bodies have a clear telos in sexual union:

- Unitive: They become one flesh (Gen 2:24); the spouses’ bodies literally join in a way that no other pairing can.

- Procreative: The very form of the act can generate life (even if not every act results in conception).

This is why SBD says sex belongs to marriage and marriage is sustained by sex: the act’s meaning (oneness) and power (life) require the covenant frame that protects, honors, and directs it. 1 Corinthians 6:16 (KJV) “What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.” Paul’s warning proves a truth: even misused sex still makes one body. If this is true with sin, how much more is it true with holy fidelity? The act is never “nothing.” It creates a bond; outside covenant it creates harm; within covenant it consummates and sustains the union.

## 4.3 Natural Law and the “Only Equation That Works”

“Sex = Marriage: The Only Equation That Works” means:

- Conjugal oneness is a reality of the body, not a mere legal fiction.

- A certificate records vows; sex consummates and sustains those vows.

- Male–male or female–female pairings cannot realize conjugal telos (no unitive+procreative form). Companionship is possible, but one-flesh conjugal union is not.

- Infertility does not negate conjugal form. Even when conception is not possible, the act remains unitive and of

procreative kind (form), preserving its covenantal meaning. Hebrews 13:4 (KJV) “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.” The honor is tied to the bed—conjugal life itself. Where the bed is honored, the covenant stands strong.

## 4.4 Intercourse: What the Word Actually Means

“Inter-course” literally denotes a between-course, a going between man and woman. The word’s historic use presumes complementarity. To redefine intercourse as anything-goes is to strip the word of its design and empty it of its covenantal dignity. SBD therefore refuses to outsource definitions to trend or taboo. We return to reality: conjugal intercourse is the exclusive marital act through which two whole persons enact and renew their covenant.

## 4.5 Pleasure: Gift to Be Stewarded

Pleasure is not the enemy; disorder is. Within marriage, pleasure is rightly enjoyed as worshipful gratitude and mutual gift—never as consumerism or coercion. John 10:10 (KJV) “I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.” Abundance here is not indulgence; it is ordered joy—the fitting enjoyment of a gift in the frame it was made for.

## 4.6 Naked and Not Ashamed: the Covenant Posture

“Naked and not ashamed” (Gen 2:25) is covenant posture, not public policy. It yields three truths for couples:

- Visibility without fear: spouses may behold one another with honor.

- Modesity: modesty is not hiding beauty; it is revealing beauty in season—for your spouse.

- Confidence by design: the body is not a mistake; it is the instrument of the covenant—to be cared for, presented with wisdom, and shared with joy.

This posture rejects both prudishness (shame at design) and pornography (shamelessness without covenant). SBD’s answer to porn is not silence; it is surpassing beauty inside the covenant.

# Chapter 5 — Sex = Marriage: The Only Equation That Works

## 5.0 Introduction

The world often presents sex and marriage as two different realities: sex as a biological or recreational act, marriage as a social or legal contract. But the SBD philosophy insists: sex is marriage by divine design, and marriage is consummated and sustained by sex. Anything less fragments God’s blueprint for oneness. As Jesus pointed back to Genesis, and Paul echoed in Corinthians, the union of man and woman is not defined by paper but by the one-flesh covenant enacted through sexual fidelity. Oneness is not imagined, symbolic, or bureaucratic—it is conjugal, physical, and spiritual.

## 5.1 Biblical Anchors of the One-Flesh Reality

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.”

> *— Genesis 2:24 (KJV)*

This first declaration defines marriage as sexual and covenantal. No certificate existed in Eden; no magistrate presided. What established oneness was the divine design of sexual union—man and wife cleaving into one flesh. “What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.”

> *— 1 Corinthians 6:16 (KJV)*

Paul’s comparison reinforces the same reality: even in sinful misuse, sex creates a one-body bond. If union with a prostitute establishes one-flesh, how much more the covenant union of husband and wife! “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.”

> *— Hebrews 13:4 (KJV)*

The honour of marriage is tied directly to the sanctity of the sexual bed. Fidelity is covenantal faithfulness expressed bodily. Defilement comes not from lack of paperwork but from misuse of the conjugal act.

## 5.2 The Only Equation That Works: 1 + 1 = 1

Culture tries false equations:

- ½ + ½ = 1 (broken halves completing each other).

- 1 + 1 + 1 = 1 (polyamory masquerading as covenant).

- 1 + 0 = 1 (self-marriage or contractual fictions).

But divine mathematics is clear: one whole man + one whole woman = one flesh.  Anything else is either arithmetic error or covenant fraud.

## 5.3.1 Fidelity Inside vs. Infidelity Outside

Infidelity outside is born of infidelity inside. Marriages collapse not because of external threats first, but because of an internal failure to cultivate sexual fidelity and intimacy. When fidelity is lived inside, temptation outside loses its power. This is why Paul warns: “Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband. The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.”

> *— 1 Corinthians 7:2–4 (KJV)*

Here fidelity is not abstract morality; it is practical covenant ownership and mutual responsibility.

## 5.3.2 The Biblical Tension Is Not “Consent vs. Coercion” — It Is Duty vs. Disorder

Here is what Scripture actually says, not modern categories: 1 Corinthians 7:2–4 (KJV) - Husbands and wives “have power” over each other’s bodies.

- The wife hath not power of her own body. - The husband hath not power of his own body. - They are commanded to “render due benevolence.” - The purpose (conjugal pleasure) will forfend fornication. - This is not a negotiation; it is covenantal obligation. √ This language is duty, not voluntarist-consent. √ It is mutual authority, not individual autonomy. √ It is the opposite of modern “my body, my choice.” √ It is the opposite of “I only give myself if I feel like it.” √ It is the opposite of “we must both be in the mood simultaneously.” √ It is the opposite of “I need emotional safety first.” Those are woke therapeutic frameworks — not biblical, not covenantal, not conjugal. (A) Conjugal Authority & Duty 1 Cor 7:2–4 - You belong to each other. - You do not have autonomous bodily rights. - Sexual giving is commanded (“render”). - Withholding is called defrauding. (B) Covenant Love, Kindness & Rhythm: hold dear-b Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cheriseth it, even as the Lord the church:  Eph 5:25–29 To Cherish is to: be fond of, to hold dear, be attacheed to, to care for, to treasure!

## 5.4 . Habit Loops, Not Certificate Loops

Certificates record vows; habits keep them.

- A paper can declare a couple married.

- Only daily sexual fidelity, affection, and pursuit keep them one flesh.

Therefore, build habit loops: These habits espouse oneness far beyond what a document alone could hold.

## 5.5 The Legal Paper vs. the Divine Covenant

Does this mean certificates are useless? No. They serve civil order, inheritance, and social recognition. But they do not constitute marriage. Paper recognizes what sex consummates. Jesus Himself validated covenant, not documents: “Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.”

> *— Matthew 19:6 (KJV)*

The divine covenant is God’s act of joining. The certificate is man’s act of recording. Confusing the two is like mistaking a photograph for the person.

## 5.6 Epicureanism Redeemed: the Pleasure Principle

Sex is not merely procreative; it is profoundly pleasurable by divine intent. Habit Category Corrected SBD Practice Tenderness gentleness, foreplay, affection, warmth, approach Conjugal Duty render to one another what is due; do not defraud (1 Cor 7:3–5) Covenant Delight Love, joy, kindness, goodness — not autonomy or withholding, delight. Pursuit never stop “dating” your spouse Celebration honour anniversaries, birthdays, and ordinary days through conjugal union

“Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.”

> *— Revelation 4:11 (KJV)*

The conjugal act, therefore, is not shameful but worshipful when expressed in covenant sexual fidelity. Pleasure is not an accident of biology but a testimony of divine design. To deprive marriage of sexual pleasure is to rob marriage of its sustaining glory.

## 5.7 Exercises for Reflection

- Scripture Meditation: Write Genesis 2:24, 1 Corinthians 6:16, and Hebrews 13:4 side by side. Compare how

each frames the one-flesh reality. What themes overlap?

- Marriage Math Journal: Reflect on your own views of the “marriage equation.” Have you believed the half-plushalf myth? How does the wholeness equation challenge you?

- Habit Loop Builder: Draft three daily or weekly practices that would strengthen your sexual fidelity with your

spouse (or, if single, prepare you to live in covenant faithfulness).

- Cultural Critique: Identify one false equation (½ + ½, 1 + 1 + 1, etc.) you see in society. Write a one-page rebuttal anchored in scripture.

## 5.8 Conclusion

Sex and marriage are not separable compartments but two words for the same covenantal reality. Marriage without sex is a contract without covenant; sex outside marriage is covenant broken by fraud. Only when the two are held together—sex = marriage—do we find the integrity of divine design. This is the only equation that works, the bedrock of fidelity, and the foundation of families that can sustain civilizations.

# Chapter 6 — The Muliebrity Baron: The Secret Power Every Wife Carries

## 6.0 Introduction: the Weight of Womanhood:

What Is Muliebrity? The State of Being Womanly Muliebrity — the state of being womanly — is not a reduction, not a weakness, and not a concession to men. It is the divinely-ordained embodiment of femininity, the secret power every wife carries into covenant. “And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.” — Genesis 2:25 (KJV) Here, womanhood is presented without apology: complete, complementary, and glorious in nakedness. The wife is designed to carry a power of attraction, presence, and influence that sustains covenant and beautifies marriage. Muliebrity is therefore the God-given condition of an adult female person, set apart to live as woman: in her body, in her temperament, in her sexuality, and in her covenant.

## 6.1 Muliebrity Defined — Design Fulfilled

The Latin muliebris means “womanly.” LAYER DESCRIPTION Outward Traits Body, attire, grooming, fashion, posture, aura. Inward Traits Temperament, reverence, emotional warmth, self-awareness, fear of the LORD. Conjugal Traits Sexual literacy, sensual openness, responsiveness, covenantal delight.

In the Sex by Design framework, muliebrity is design fulfilled. Muliebrity is not imitation of masculinity; it is not competition with masculinity. It is the flourishing of the female design — and therein lies its covenantal power. “Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come. She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” — Proverbs 31:25-26 (KJV) This is the woman SBD is training: strong yet submitted, wise yet reverent, alluring yet holy — fully, unapologetically woman.

## 6.2 Woman by Design — Adult Female Person

To speak of muliebrity, we must say plainly what woman is. A woman, in this covenant context, is an adult human female by creation — not by mood, not by vote, not by trend — but by design. Her body testifies:

- she is formed to receive and respond,

- her breasts, hips, and womb proclaim capacity for nurture and life,

- her cycles tell time, seasons, and fertility.

Her soul and temperament, shaped in holiness, are called to:

- gentleness without weakness,

- courage without rivalry,

- wisdom without hardness.

Her sexuality is not random appetite; it is womanly orientation toward her husband: to receive him, answer him, delight him, and stand with him in covenant. “Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.” — Song of Solomon 4:5 (KJV) The Song of Songs is not embarrassed by her body; it honours her womanliness as beauty, as garden, as delight.  SBD refuses to be more ashamed of womanly form than Scripture is.

## 6.3 Womanliness As the Basis of Marriage

Marriage is not built on neutrality; it is built on womanliness and manliness meeting in covenant. - Muliebrity is therefore not extra; it is foundation. - A wife relates to her husband as woman, not as generic person. - Her womanliness shapes how she attracts, receives, responds, and supports. - Her attire, scent, voice, touch, and timing are all part of her covenant ministry.

- Her husband is not marrying “someone”; he is marrying a woman — and SBD insists that wives must be taught to know, value, and deploy their womanliness. When a wife denies or neglects muliebrity, she is not being “strong”; she is emptying the marriage of one of its pillars. When she embraces it rightly, she turns her home into a place where covenant, sexuality, and civilization meet.

## 6.4 Muliebrity and Submission — the Matrimonial Order

Ephesians 5:22–24 (KJV) “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body. Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” In The Matrimonial Order (SBD), this passage is unpacked with precision:

- The adverb “as” means to the same degree, equally, every bit. It qualifies the submission clause.

- “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands as unto the Lord”: if a wife is not submitted to the Lord, this

verse is not yet attainable for her, because she lacks the pattern.

- “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”: the word “even” intensifies the

comparison. The husband’s headship is not symbolic; it is positional.

- “Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing”: Scripture

closes loopholes. This is not a suggestion; it is order. Muliebrity, then, is womanly submission rightly lived: not silence, not slavery, but a clear, conscious, joyful yielding to the husband’s headship, as unto the Lord. No system can be built without leadership. True Matrimoney does not apologise for headship; it teaches wives how to live under it with honour, wisdom, and power.

## 6.5 The Proverbs 31 Portrait — Character and Work

Proverbs 31:10-12 (KJV) “Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil. She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.”

Here, womanliness is trustworthy, industrious, and oriented toward her husband’s good. She is economically active, physically strong, spiritually alert, and domestically excellent. Muliebrity is not vibes; it is virtue in motion. It is womanliness lived in the fear of the LORD: “Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.” — Proverbs

## 31:30 (KJV)

The Muliebrity Baron knows:

- her womanliness is not negotiable,

- her submission is not optional

- her power is not in rivalry but in reverent, womanly excellence before God and before her husband.

## 6.5 A — Form and Fitness: the Stewardship of the Female Body

Romans 12:1 (KJV) ARE A

## Prov. 31 Expression

## Muliebrity Aplication

Character “Virtuous… price far above rubies.” Moral solidity; she cannot be cheaply bought. Trustworthiness “The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her.” She is not secretive, double-hearted, or manipulative. Industry “She seeketh wool… worketh willingly… planteth a vineyard.” She is not idle; she builds value. Strength “She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.” She cares for her body and capacity to work. Household Care “She looketh well to the ways of her household.” She manages atmosphere, rhythm, food, order. Speech “In her tongue is the law of kindness.” Her words are disciplined, not destructive. Honour “Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.” Recognition follows her faithfulness over time.

“I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Muliebrity is not only moral and emotional grace; it is embodied order. The womanly form is a trust. Her hips, waist, carriage, and poise were crafted to express attraction, fertility, and beauty within covenant. To neglect her form is to dim one of the lights God placed in her to bless her husband and adorn her marriage. “Thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes. I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof.” — Song of Solomon 7:7-8 (KJV) Scripture does not blush at attraction; it ennobles and commands it. A wife’s physical allure is covenantal capital, not vanity. To keep herself fit and appealing is an act of fidelity and reverence — an honour to her husband, an act of worship to her Maker, and a protection to her home. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Article 16 § 1) affirms that “men and women of full age have the right to marry.” Marriage is for the mature — those who can master appetite, emotion, and body. Physical maturity without discipline breeds decay; disciplined maturity creates enduring delight. Therefore, the Muliebrity Baron guards her femininity with all diligence: she nourishes, trains, and adorns her body for self and hence for covenant celebration. DOMAIN

## Practice & Purpose

Fitness Maintain health, tone, and stamina. Discipline appetite and activity; steward energy for service and delight. Form Honour posture, grooming, and scent. Walk with composure; keep the body graceful and responsive. Femininity Preserve softness without weakness — fit, supple, and elegant. Seductive only toward her husband. Stewardship Reject neglect and excess alike. Obesity and disorder dull desire and reduce capacity for conjugal joy.

## 6.6 Dressing for Nakedness: the Nakedness Genre

Genesis 2:25 (KJV) “And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.” Nakedness is not shameful — it is primal literacy. Before there were fabrics, there was flesh. Before there were wardrobes, there was womanhood. Muliebrity is not about hiding nakedness but stewarding it. The question is not “How well do you cover?” but “How well do you manage your nakedness?” Ask yourself —

- Do I keep it clean always?

- Do I dress against it or for it?

- Do I use it for or against my husband?

- Am I afraid of it, or do I steward it?

The Muliebrity Fashion House calls this the nakedness genre of dressing:

- Dressing around nakedness.

- Dressing with nakedness.

- Dressing for nakedness.

- Dressing naked.

The purpose is not vulgar exposure but covenantal allure — seeing something but seeing nothing, the art of suggestion without shame, the crown of feminine power. Sexuality as Formulaic Literacy

- Is arousal triggered by nakedness? Yes.

- Can greater arousal be triggered by dressing naked? Yes.

The allure is in balance: beauty serves nakedness; clothing serves sexuality. Dresses did not precede nakedness — they exist to serve it. To bury nakedness under fabric is to deny its covenantal power. “Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for Thou hast created all things, and for Thy pleasure they are and were created.” — Revelation 4:11 (KJV) Pleasure is divine. Clothing exists to steward pleasure, not stifle it.

## 6.7 Hygiene, Aura, and Presence

Muliebrity is more than dress — it is aura: the fragrance, discipline, and glow that radiates from within.

- Hygiene: Cleanliness is covenantal respect. A neglected body is a neglected covenant.

- Aura: The atmosphere a woman carries — her voice, her scent, her composure — is her signature.

- Presence: To enter a room and alter it by grace, elegance, and confidence is muliebrity in motion.

## 6.8 Practical Drills

- Wardrobe Audit: Categorize every outfit under the four muliebrity packs. Which pack is strongest? Which is weakest?

- Nakedness Reflection: Journal your answers to the nakedness questions above.

- Aura Practice: Spend a week cultivating presence — posture, smile, fragrance, composure — and note how your

husband responds.

- Scriptural Meditation: Read Proverbs 31:25–30 daily. Journal one trait to embody each day.

## 6.9 Conclusion — the Secret Power Every Wife Carries

Muliebrity is not accidental; it is design — a form of covenantal literacy, the way a wife communicates attraction, reverence, and power through body, dress, aura, and presence. A woman fully alive in her muliebrity is not a liability but a force. She is the secret power that beautifies covenant and sustains marriage.

# Chapter 7 — The Virility Baron: Authority Through Service and Manhood

Virility is covenantal presence, divine authority, and masculine stewardship. If muliebrity is the crown of womanhood, virility is the staff of manhood — to guide, guard, and give life. Scripture anchors this order: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

> *— Ephesians 5:23 (KJV)*

Headship is not optional. It is divine assignment. The question is not whether man will lead, but whether he will lead in covenantal fidelity or abdicate his place.

## The Virility Baron: Authority Through Service and Manhood

## 7.0 The World of Virility

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.”

> *— Ephesians 5:25 (KJV)*

This is not a soft verse; it is a kingly one. Virility is the world of manhood by design — the realm where a man stands in his full charge before God, before his wife, before his children, and before his generation. It is the heat of his blood, the weight of his presence, the sharpness of his mind, and the bowing of his spirit to Yahweh. But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. 1 Corinthians 11:3 (KJV)

Virility is not an afterthought of creation; it is a strategic axis of civilization. Men were set as heads, not as accidents; as givers, not as ornaments; as carriers of weight, not as spectators. When virility is trained, covenant flourishes. When virility is absent, everything thins and collapses. This chapter is not an apology for men. It is a coronation — the awakening of the Virility Baron, the man whose strength blesses, whose sexuality is glory, whose leadership gives life, and whose authority is service by design.

## 7.1 Virility — Name, Root, and Scope

The word virility comes from the Latin vir — man — the same root as virtus (virtue, excellence, strength) and virtuosity (skilful power). At the root, virility assumes vigour, potency, and worth. In covenant terms, virility is: The God-given, manly vitality to generate, protect, and sustain life — expressed through physical strength, mental courage, sexual power, and spiritual headship, ordered toward covenant joy and dominion in abundant living. It includes: o male sexuality (drive, potency, pursuit, arousal, seed) o male fitness (strength, stamina, muscle, resilience) o male psychology (focus, courage, self-command) o male spirituality (priesthood, headship, covering) o male presence (how he walks, looks, smells, speaks, and rules) Virility is not a problem to be solved; it is a glory to be revealed and stewarded.

## 7.2 Identity Is Formed by Design, Not by Warnings

Modern discourse often tries to define masculinity by negation, by a long list of what men must not be: “Virility is not X…” “Virility is not bravado…” “Virility is not a wildfire…” Even if the intent behind those lines is to clarify, the effect is: √ reductive √ defensive √ passive

√ subtly apologetic √ subtly emasculating and yes — it echoes the modern, woke moral lens that pathologises male identity before affirming it: We reject this tone. This book is not written to correct men’s existence; it is written to awaken men to their design, their authority, their glory, and their covenant calling. In covenant anthropology: Identity is formed by design, not by warnings. Adam did not become man through a lecture on what not to be. He became man when God formed him, breathed into him, tasked him, and presented him with woman. Man was designed to lead, not apologise. Man was designed to initiate, not retreat. Man was designed to pierce, plant, provide, and protect — without shame. Man was designed to burn with sexuality and strength, not to be neutered by suspicion. Warnings are second-rate to the espousal of his design, but they can never form a man. Design forms him to respond to Purpose & Covenant; design instruct him to function aright; design is sheer. SBD therefore speaks to virility as gift, power, and glory — not as a danger to be managed but as a flame to be rightly fed.

## 7.3 Epistemology — How We Know What Virility Is

We know what virility is by three witnesses:

## 7.3.1 . Revelation — Scripture gives the blueprint:

Adam charged to work and keep the garden (Genesis 2:15). Husband set as head of the wife (Ephesians 5:23). Husband commanded to love, nourish, and cherish as Christ (Ephesians 5:25–29). Men charged to “quit you like men, be strong” (1 Corinthians 16:13).

## 7.3.2 . Creation Design — The male body:

larger bone structure, muscle potential, hormonal profile sexual drive oriented outward and forward capacity to impregnate, to lift, to shield, to endure

## 7.3.3 . Fruit and History — Wherever male vitality and headship are rightly honoured:

√ families stabilise √ nations hold √ women flourish √ children grow straight Virility is not a social construction; it is a revealed and visible design constant.

## 7.4 Ontology — What Virility Is in Itself

Ontologically, virility is manhood in motion — male being turned into male doing. It is: - Physical: the embodied capacity to labour, fight, sire, and endure - Psychological/Moral: the inner steel that chooses courage, discipline, and responsibility - Spiritual/Covenantal: the headship that leads, blesses, and covers in Yahweh’s name Virility is not mere potential. It is presence: the felt reality that a man is here, awake, engaged, ready.

## 7.5 Axiology — What Virility Values

The values of virility are the rails on which male power runs. They do not deny pleasure; they assume he must know it, master it, and provide it. A virile man values: - Truth over illusion — he lives from reality, not from fantasy or fashion, but he understands that appearance is part of reality; how he looks and presents himself affects everyone he leads. - Hedonism rightly ordered — he is devoted to pleasure as God designed it: he must understand comfort, joy, and delight in his own body and soul so he can sire a household of comfort, joy, and delight. A man who has never tasted ordered pleasure cannot steward it for others.

- Duty and delight together — he bears responsibility and he experiences it as honour; he does not choose between duty and joy. He finds his joy in doing his duty. - Fidelity of the whole self — he is faithful with his sexuality, his strength, his money, his emotions. - Fruit over noise — he measures his life not by labels but by outcomes: a joyful wife, confident children, ordered finances, effective work, a warm and holy home. A virile man does not fear pleasure. He understands that to provide joy, he must understand it. He must know comfort to create comfort. He must know ecstasy to shepherd it. He must practice hedonism rightly in himself to lead a hedonistic (joy-filled, pleasure-ordered) covenant.

## 7.6 Physical Virility — Strength, Stamina, Sexual Presence

The male body is not neutral; it is an instrument of rulership, work, and conjugal glory. A virile man honours his frame, hormones, and drive as gifts.

## 7.6.1 Strength and Stamina

Fitness is not a walk in the park. It is training for kingship. The man’s body must be: - fit to steward sexuality in marriage as a sexual relationship, not just to respond to it or request it - strong enough to lift and carry real weight - conditioned enough to work long and recover well - agile enough to respond in crisis - resilient enough to endure stress Foundational Training Pattern (Minimum Standard) 3 sessions per week, 60–75 minutes each, plus targeted running and active movement on other days. Session A — Strength (Lower Body + Core) - Back squat or front squat - Deadlift or Romanian deadlift - Lunges or step-ups - Core carries (farmer’s walk, suitcase carry, front carry)

Session B — Strength (Upper Body) - Bench press or weighted push-ups - Pull-ups or heavy rows - Overhead press - Dips or close-grip pressing Session C — Conditioning and Power - Kettlebell swings - Loaded carries - Short sprints or explosive bodyweight circuits (push, pull, jump, crawl) Session D — Running Protocol At least 3 times a week, on separate days or after lighter strength work: - Minimum 45 minutes per session - Minimum 3 miles (≈ 5 km), building up as fitness grows - Mix of steady-state runs and one weekly session with intervals (e.g. 5×3-minute hard runs with 2-minute easy jog between) Running stretches lungs, heart, and mental endurance. A man who can run far and lift heavy is ready, in body, for virile stewardship of work, crisis, and conjugal passion. Support disciplines: - Protein-forward nutrition; minimal junk and intoxication - 7–8 hours of sleep - One full rest day weekly - Daily mobility 10–15 minutes A man who trains his body trains his will. The same discipline that builds muscle builds headship and sexual stamina.

## 7.6.2 Sexual Presence and Wardrobes (A3 + Mv Fashion House)

Sexuality is not only what a man does in bed; it is how he shows up everywhere.

SBD’s A3 framework — Attitude, Attire, Allure — is the grammar of male sexuality. ATTITUDE He carries himself as man: - confident but not crude - warm but not weak - focused but not tense His eyes communicate interest; his posture says “I am able; I am willing; I am present.” His wife sees him and feels chosen, claimed, and safe.

## Attire — the Mv Fashion House Wardrobes

Clothing is not an apology; it is amplified design. The MV Fashion House (M = Muliebrity, V = Virility) curates wardrobes that express male sexuality and authority across every sphere: - Casual Outdoor Pack: fitted, masculine silhouettes; fabrics that show he is alive, strong, and ready to move. She sees him in public and remembers him in private. - Home-Comfort Pack (for himself): relaxed but presentable, never sloppy. Even resting, he looks like a man, not a boy. - Covenant Allure Pack (for his wife): deliberately sensual pieces — fitted tees or shirts, body-conscious lounge wear, unbuttoned collars, bare forearms — that highlight his frame, chest, shoulders, back. These are chosen for her eyes, to make him visually irresistible at home. - Corporate Wardrobe: sharp lines, structured jackets, clean shoes, intentional accessories. His masculinity is pressed and polished; he looks like decision and direction. - Official / Ceremony Wardrobe: elevated versions for ministry, ceremonies, and public leadership; fabrics and cuts that communicate weight and honour. - Night Casual Pack: soft, intimate fabrics close to skin; he looks approachable, touchable, and desirable in the hours when covenant hedonism is most likely to bloom. Attire is theology in fabric: it preaches that man and woman are sexual by design, and that this sexuality belongs in covenant splendour.

ALLURE Allure is the fragrance and texture of his presence: - Grooming: beard or clean shave, but always deliberate; hair managed, not abandoned - Scent: chosen, memorable, associated in her mind with safety and arousal - Voice: calm, warm, and commanding; he does not whine or shrink — he calls, invites, leads Sexual presence is the sum of A3: Attitude, Attire, Allure. A virile man uses all three to say to his wife without words: “You are desired. I am ready. This covenant is alive.”

## 7.7 Psychological and Moral Virility — Mind, Will, Resolve

Virility is not only in the muscles; it is in the mindset. A virile man is: - Courageous — he faces, he does not flee - Decisive — he can choose and own the consequences - Self-commanded — appetite, speech, and temper obey him - Mission-driven — he lives by assignment, not drift - Resilient — he bends in storms but does not break Daily mental practice: - Fixed wake time; no snooze - Scripture and reflection before screens - One hard task completed before 10:00 a.m. - No complaining; only problem-solving or silence - When wrong, he says, “That was my fault,” and adjusts

## 7.8 Spiritual and Covenantal Virility — the Divine Matrimonial Rule

Virility reaches its highest expression in covenant headship.

Asexuality in a marriage covenant is not neutral; it is a break from design. Many side effects (like porn and fantasy) flourish because real-world sexuality is underfed and undereducated. The SBD answer is not to obsess over side effects, but to fill the covenant with the good: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.”

So we focus on: - educated sexuality - courageous seduction - mutual responsiveness

- ongoing exploration within holiness SBD’s other works — The Arts of Marriage: The Art of Seduction, The Art of Sexuality, The Art of the Wife, etc. — expand these domains. Here, the Virility Baron is charged simply and clearly: Know, enjoy, and lead your conjugal life as king — not as a guest.

The husband’s sexual leadership means: - he does not withdraw - he does not starve the covenant bed - he does not live as if he were a brother, not a bridegroom - he is present, ready, imaginative, gentle, strong, and warm “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband. The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.”

Two bodies, one claim, one joy.

Virility forms household government. Roles gathered in one man: - Prophet: names reality, casts vision, sets direction - Priest: administers the divine — complete meditation, devotion, and the ministry of the Word to his family; he is the living link between Scripture and the rhythm of the home

# Chapter 8 — Pics & Pearls: The Beauty of Nakedness vs. the Lies of Porn

## 8.1 Introduction: Nakedness, Marriage, and Allure

“And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.” (Genesis 2:25, KJV) Genesis 2:25 is the fountainhead of marital meaning. Nakedness here is not a mood that came and went; it is the original disposition of marriage—the usual, covenantal atmosphere of husband and wife. Before fabric there was flesh; before shame there was sight; before culture there was creation. The atmosphere of marriage is nakedness without shame. Scripture trains the imagination to honor that atmosphere, not cheapen it. Song of Songs gives us the liturgy of marital allure:

- “Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.” (Song 1:2, KJV)

- “My beloved is mine, and I am his.” (Song 2:16, KJV)

- “I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.” (Song 7:10, KJV)

These are not trivial lines; they are curriculum for covenant desire. They sanctify nakedness by giving it language, cadence, and permanence. In this light, marital allure is liturgy—a covenantal way of seeing and being seen, speaking and being spoken to. The logical frame:

- Premise 1 (Gen 2:24): Marriage is a one-flesh covenant.

- Premise 2 (Gen 2:25): The one-flesh covenant is lived in nakedness without shame.

- Premise 3 (1 Cor 6:16): “The two… shall be one flesh” is realized sexually.

- Conclusion: Nakedness belongs essentially to marriage; marriage = nakedness = sexuality (in covenant).

This is not “warning language”; it is definition. To minister one’s naked attraction to one’s spouse is pastoral work inside the home. It teaches the body to tell the truth: “We belong to one another.” Over time, the couple forms covenantal memory—a private gallery of glances, gestures, wardrobes, and rituals that beautify loyalty.

Practical entailments (covenantal):

- Household imagery: what you wear for each other, how you greet, the ambience you set, the rhythm of the evening—

these are not random; they are marital pedagogy.

- Covenant keepsakes: private photography or mementos kept strictly between spouses function as pearls—memory anchors of delight and belonging.

- Song-language: “My beloved is mine…” is not quaint; it is training for desire within marriage.

In short, light defines itself. When couples steward imagery as covenant, counterfeits have nothing left to colonize. Nakedness is not an embarrassment to outsource; it is a calling to steward.

## 8.2 Nakedness As the Objective Reality (COPULA Analysis, Fully Explained)

“And they WERE both naked, the man and his wife, and WERE not ashamed.” (Genesis 2:25, KJV)

## 8.2.1 What Is a “Copula,” and Why Does “Were” Matter?

In logic and grammar, a copula is the linking verb (usually “to be”) that connects a subject (S) to its predicate (P) to assert identity, state, or essential attribute. It is the hinge that says, “This subject is/was this predicate.”

- Here, S = “the man and his wife.”

- P = “naked and not ashamed.”

- Copula = “WERE,” asserting that P truly belongs to S.

So the verse does not describe a passing incident (“they happened to be undressed”). The repeated WERE makes a formal assertion: nakedness without shame is the constitutive state of husband and wife.

## 8.2.2 Four Functions of the Copula in Gen 2:25

- Attribute, not accident — how?

Because the copula links S to P as a truth claim. The sentence structure is not adjectival fluff; it is ontological assertion. It does not say, “They tried nudity,” but “they WERE naked… and WERE not ashamed”—the state inherently belongs to the marital subject.

- Syllogism clarified:

- Major: What the copula predicates to S, belongs to S as true.

- Minor: The copula predicates “naked and not ashamed” to “the man and his wife.”

- Conclusion: Nakedness without shame belongs to the marital subject as its proper state.

- Foundation, not ornament — how?

In Scripture’s creation order, marriage is the basis of family, and family is the fundamental unit of society (UDHR 16). If the copula predicates nakedness without shame as intrinsic to marriage, then that predicate is civilizational. To strip nakedness (without shame) from marriage is to weaken the family’s foundation—hence social looseness follows.

- Objective fact, not preference — how?

The mood is indicative (facts), not subjunctive (wishes) nor imperative (commands). Scripture states what is: “they WERE”—not “they ought to be,” “they felt,” or “they became.” The grammar communicates objective ontology: the marital state is nakedness without shame.

- Joins, not just describes — how?

The copula does more than attribute; in the creation context it joins S to P as one reality. Genesis 2:24 defines the oneflesh union; Paul expounds it as sexual joining (1 Cor 6:16). Thus, “they WERE naked… and not ashamed” is not a mannequin tableau; it signals lived union—nakedness that expresses the sexual reality of the one flesh in covenant. Therefore (your identity statement, preserved): Marriage = Nakedness = Sexuality (in covenant).

- Clarification you requested:

- Nakedness is not a threat to fidelity; it is fidelity’s environment. Learning to be and dress for nakedness before marriage (as education in design, not as fornication) builds health, not promiscuity. Nakedness ≠ sin; the fallen state and under-education cause misuse.

- Sexuality (our created sexual nature) is good. The misuse is sex as an act severed from covenant, not “having sexuality” itself. So we say: Sex (the act) without covenant misuses a holy power. Sexuality (nature) is the divine basis from which

marriage arises.

## 8.2.3 Marital Allure in One Line

“Marital allure is the ministry of your naked attraction to your spouse (both naked: Gen 2:25)— or you will let something else do the ministry for you.” This is not “being against” something; it is being for creation’s order. Where marriages abdicate stewardship of imagery, counterfeits step in. That is the burden of Marriage = Porn & Beyond: not to praise pornography, but to prove that marriage alone is designed to supply what porn pretends to offer—attention, arousal, aesthetic delight—rightly ordered toward fidelity and fruitfulness.

## 8.2.4 Illustrations (COVENANTAL, Not Prurient)

- Wardrobe as literacy: Wives dress for their nakedness (not against it); husbands dress their authority attractively.

Clothing serves sexuality; it does not bury it.

- Atmosphere as pedagogy: Set a weekly “Song of Songs hour.” Read aloud (Song 1:2; 2:16; 7:10). Let Scripture tutor

your speech and mood.

- Pearls journal: Record phrases, moments, shared looks that became anchors of desire and reassurance—a gallery of

covenant. Retained insights, now seated in the logic

- Covenant trust: no shame, no hiding—nakedness without shame is trust codified.

- Stewardship, not suppression: not “How much did you cover?” but “How well do you manage your nakedness?”

- Light, not reaction: define the home by creation, not by reacting to corruption. Counterfeits fade when truth is practiced.

Song of Songs re-anchored as curriculum

- 2:16 — Belonging language dignifies allure.

- 7:10 — Desire as covenantal, not worldly.

- 1:2 — Speech as allure; verbal affection is part of marital nakedness.

## 8.3 Covenant Literacy & Image Stewardship

Thesis: In marriage, the body speaks a covenant language. Stewarding imagery is literacy—learning to “read” and “write” fidelity with presence, attire, speech, and atmosphere. Biblical anchors

- “They were both naked… and were not ashamed.” (Gen 2:25) — nakedness is the covenant’s mother tongue.

- “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth… let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be

thou ravished always with her love.” (Proverbs 5:18–19, KJV) — desire directed by covenant.

- “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband… Defraud ye

not one the other…” (1 Corinthians 7:3–5, KJV) — stewardship, reciprocity, and agreed rhythms. Principles of stewardship

- Representation: Spouses carry each other’s honor in public. Dress, speech, and demeanor should say, “I am my

beloved’s” (Song 7:10).

- Confidentiality: Imagery is for the covenant, not for crowds. Keep it private, sacred, and protected.

- Consent & cadence: Desire is holy; its expression is mutual, kind, and rhythmic (1 Cor 7:5).

- Formation: Repetition trains affection. Small rituals (a specific scent, a greeting at the door, a weekly reading)

catechize the senses for fidelity. Household canon for imagery

- Set language norms: affectionate names; gratitude before critique.

- Set presentation norms: clean, intentional, attractive at home; dignified in public.

- Set technology norms: anything captured remains private, encrypted, and mutually owned.

## 8.4 The Redemption of Desire: Light Before Darkness

Desire is not the problem; dis-order is. Scripture redeems desire by giving it a home—marriage. Full citations

- “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth… let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be

thou ravished always with her love.” (Proverbs 5:18–19, KJV)

- “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled…” (Hebrews 13:4, KJV)

Claims

- Desire is sacred when ordered to covenant.

- Desire is educable: imagination can be discipled by Scripture (Song 1:2; 2:16; 7:10).

- Desire is fruitful when anchored in exclusivity (Gen 2:24–25).

Practice (light-first approach)

- Fill the home with lighted examples: speech, music, scent, attire, touch—so the body learns truth and forgets counterfeits.

- Establish gratitude rituals that turn desire into praise, not complaint.

- Use Scripture aloud during courtship-evenings to retrain imagination toward holiness and joy.

## 8.5 Dressing for Nakedness

## (INTEGRATED With Muliebrity & Virility)

Design axiom: Clothing exists for nakedness as language exists for meaning—to reveal truth, not erase it. Muliebrity (womanliness)

- Nakedness genre (Muliebrity Fashion House):

- Dressing around nakedness — silhouette honored, not hidden.

- Dressing with nakedness — fabrics that serve form.

- Dressing for nakedness — attire that sets a covenantal mood.

- Dressing naked — unashamed intimacy for your husband alone.

- Self-questions: Do I clean it always? Do I dress for my nakedness? Is my wardrobe serviceable to covenant? Do I

use it for, not against, my husband?

Virility (manliness)

- Fit, grooming, presence, and scent are covenant communications.

- A3 Model (Attitude → Attire → Allure): authority expressed through service, confidence without arrogance, and

strength with tenderness (Eph 5:25–29). Guardrails (defined in-covenant)

- Misuse is not elegance; it is exporting what belongs to covenant into public consumption.

- Fidelity in fabric means: avoid wardrobes that bury nakedness in neglect, or broadcast what belongs to the

marriage bed.

- Goal: attraction inside, dignity outside.

“Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.” (Song 4:7, KJV)

## 8.6 Practical Drills: Cultivating Daily Allure

- Allure Calendar: One evening weekly for Scripture, conversation, and presentation.

- Song of Songs Hour: Read 1:2, 2:16, 7:10 aloud; practice covenant speech.

- Wardrobe Labs: Build “muliebrity packs” (home, outdoors, corporate, intimacy). Build “virility packs” (daily,

work, date, sanctuary).

- Pearls Journal: Record phrases, gestures, looks that deepened trust or desire.

- Scent & Sound: Choose a shared scent and playlist that “belongs” to your covenant evenings.

- Consent Signals: Create simple signals for pursue/slow/stop—kindness increases frequency.

- Technology Ethic: If you capture private imagery, store it encrypted; mutual consent only; never shared.

- Anniversary Archive: Curate a private album of memories (notes, vows, tokens).

- Aftercare Ritual: Post-intimacy gratitude (two sentences each).

- Conflict Reset: When tempers cool, read Eph 5:25–29 & 33 together; pray briefly; schedule repair.

- Travel Mode: Pack one “for-nakedness” set each when apart; exchange devoted notes.

- Sabbath of Delight: Once a month, a longer evening: slow dinner, bath, prayer, reading, unhurried intimacy.

## 8.7 Pics & Pearls: Imagery, Devotion, Legacy

Pearls are covenant memories—the kept language of belonging.

- Devotion: Treat imagery as liturgy. Open the Pearls Journal on anniversaries; re-speak vows; read Song 2:16 and

7:10 aloud.

- Discretion: “Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel…” (Matt 5:15) — but they also do not parade it in the street. Keep pearls private and precious.

- Legacy (to yourselves): You are writing the marriage you will remember. Couples who forget beauty become functional roommates; couples who remember beauty become lifelong lovers.

“Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.” (Song 1:2, KJV) “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.” (Heb 13:4a, KJV) Final claim: Pornography will not have the last word; covenant beauty will. Pics & Pearls is not about chasing images but curating memory—training your eyes and hearts to see as God saw in Eden: naked, and not ashamed.
