# Chapter 11 — Practice From Perfection: Living Out Conjugal Fidelity

## 11.0 The Principle of Origin: You Practice Because You Are Perfect

Humanity was not created broken. Humanity was created whole. Humanity was created holy. Humanity was created teleios—complete, entire, lacking nothing. “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness… So God created man in His own image… male and female created He them.”

> *— Genesis 1:26–28*

This is not symbolic language. This is not metaphor. This is ontology—the truth of being before the distortion of becoming. We were made in the likeness of God, not partially, not incrementally, not potentially, but perfectly: - fully formed, - morally whole, - structurally complete, - teleologically fitted,

- relationally competent. Creation did not begin with damage. Creation began with design—with completeness.

## Holiness Is Origin, Not Aspiration

Why does God say: “Be holy, for I am holy”? Because holiness is not a target — it is your template. Why does Jesus declare: “Be perfect (teleioi), as your Father in heaven is perfect”? (Matt. 5:48) Because the word “be” does not mean become. Etymology of “Be” - Old English: beon — to exist, to remain, to abide - Proto-Germanic: beunan — to be in a state - Definition: to stand in what already is; to manifest what is extant To “be perfect” means: - Exist from perfection. - Operate from completeness. - Express your original state. - Live from the truth of your nature. It does not mean “attempt perfection.” It means “act according to what you already are.”

## Teleios Is Wholeness, Completeness, Perfection

The biblical word teleios (g5046) means: - whole - complete

- perfect - brought to its proper end - fully developed in nature and function It is not flawlessness in the shallow, modern sense. It is perfection in the eternal, ontological sense — the state of being fully fitted for your created purpose. Teleios is not a goal. Teleios is your Genesis. “As He is, so are we in this world.”

> *— 1 John 4:17*

Not “as He will be,” not “as we hope to be,” but as He is — so are we. This is the anthropology of perfection. This is why humanity hungers for excellence. This is why conscience convicts. This is why the soul rejects moral mediocrity. We were not made for halfness. We were not made for incompletion. Perfection is the cause; practice is the effect.

A perfect marriage is not two incomplete souls trying to fill each other’s emptiness. A perfect marriage is two complete persons expressing the completeness God gave them. God did not say: “Two halves shall become one half.” He said: “The two shall become one flesh.” (Gen. 2:24) This is whole + whole = one whole. A fraction cannot create a whole. Only a whole can unite into wholeness.

Just as: - A cow cannot hiss because hissing is not its nature, - A human cannot escape the call to perfection because perfection is its nature. We expect perfection because we were created perfect. We desire order because we were designed ordered. We hunger for excellence because excellence is our essence. Marriage does not transform broken people into whole ones. Marriage requires whole ones. Two teleios persons → one teleios covenant.

## Practice Flows From Perfection

This is the SBD axiom:

## **PERFECTION (TELEIOS) Is the Given State.

## Practice Is the Expression of the Given.

We practice FROM a perfect state, not toward one.** - Perfection → identity - Practice → manifestation - Failure to practice → denial of given perfection (“Faith without works is dead.”) You do not practice to become perfect. You practice because you are perfect. You practice fidelity because fidelity is your nature. You practice holiness because holiness is your origin. You practice devotion because devotion is your design. Your actions do not create identity; your actions reveal identity. Practice is not self-improvement — practice is self-expression. Practice is the outward life interpreting the inward truth. Practice is perfection taking on ritual, rhythm, and reality.

This is why marriage requires practice: Not to manufacture what is missing, but to express what is extant. We practice perfection because we ARE perfect; we do not practice to become what God already made us.

## 11.1 The Logic of Formation & Practice

If perfection is origin, then practice is ontology in motion. A covenant does not survive by sentiment; it survives by formation — the repeated expression of what is true. Fidelity is not a one-time promise. Fidelity is a rhythm. Fidelity is a discipline. Fidelity is a muscle. “By reason of use their senses are exercised to discern both good and evil.”

> *— Hebrews 5:14*

Practice is the reason-of-use principle: truth exercised until it becomes instinct; devotion rehearsed until it becomes reflex; love embodied until it becomes fluency. Let me restate the above insight in its purest logical form: If perfection is origin, and teleios is inherent, and instinct means inborn pattern, then nothing inherent needs to “become” what it already is. What is precise and correct: **Truth does not need repetition to “become” instinct.

Truth IS instinct — repetition is simply the environment where instinct EXPRESSes itself.** **Devotion does not need to become a reflex. Devotion IS the reflex — practice reveals the reflex.** **Love does not need to become fluency. Love IS fluency — practice is the operation of that fluency. This  hermeneutic is flawless and consistent with: - Genesis 1:26–28 (origin perfection), - Matthew 5:48 (existential command), - 1 John 4:17 (as He is, so are we), - Hebrews 5:14 (exercise reveals, not creates), - Romans 12 (renewal = expression, not manufacture), - Proverbs 23:7 (“as a man thinketh… so is he”). SBD Principle: FIRST: WHAT IS FORMATION in SBD? **Formation ≠ Fixing. Formation ≠ Becoming something you are not. Formation ≠ improvement.** (These are the worldly/woke definitions.) In Sex by Design, formation is: **FORMATION = Education in the Truth of Your Nature. WHAT IS PRACTICE in SBD? Practice is: **the consistent enactment of your nature. Perfection lived out. Perfection exercised.

Perfection expressed.** You don’t practice to become perfect. You practice because you are perfect.

Because truth is nature, not mood: “My conduct obeys my identity, not my impulses.” Behavior expresses teleios because: - wholeness produces steadiness - integrity follows ontology - covenant manifests naturally where identity is known Behavioral expression = the body remembering what the soul already is.

2 — Temperamental Expression (Virtue as the Default Tone) Temperament is not something to “fix”; it is something to recognize and govern. Teleios temperament is: - steadiness over volatility - gentleness over agitation - tone as truth, not reaction A mature spouse does not “become” tender; they manifest tenderness because tenderness is inherent to teleios nature. Teleios Temperament Formula: Tension → Tenderness Difference → Discernment Pressure → Peace This is not improvement.

They need to be seated correctly. “Emotion in wholeness amplifies truth; emotion in ignorance dethrones it.” Teleios emotional expression: - magnifies good - stabilizes affection - deepens intimacy - refuses to weaponize pain Emotional purity is not emotional suppression; it is emotional alignment.

Perfection is not an event — it is expressed daily. Marriage is not sustained by occasional intensity; it is sustained by consistent identity.**

## 11.3 Practice As Teleios Proof

Teleios maturity reveals itself under repetition. What you repeat reveals what you revere. Practice is not the creation of perfection; it is the confirmation of it. A teleios couple understands: A mature couple does not wait for passion — they cultivate it. They do not wait for peace — they practice it. They do not wait for affection — they express it. They do not wait for understanding — they pursue it. SBD Axiom: “Peace is not a gift received; it is a discipline sustained.” Practice = Perfection in Motion.
